factors.name: Variant diversity and entropy
factors.summary: The normalized EPA sequence entropies, n_variants, heterogeneity_rate_variants and most Entropies measures load positively (about 0.85–0.94), while the top-k variant ratios, ratio_most_common_variant and std_variant_occurrence load negatively. The factor separates logs with many evenly spread variants from logs dominated by a few variants. It is the largest factor (28% of variance) and also attracts weaker loadings from minimum and mode trace length, distinct_activities_min and complexity_factor; several DFG measures cross-load on it at about 0.53–0.56.

factors.name: Log volume and trace length
factors.summary: Activity occurrence statistics, n_events, typical trace length (median, q3, geometric mean), the unnormalized EPA entropies, average_edit_distance and lempel_ziv_complexity load at about 0.70–0.91, and event_density loads at -0.68. The factor reflects how many events a log contains and how long its traces are. This size reading assumes a constant number of traces, which holds here because n_traces was removed as constant.

factors.name: Activity alphabet and trace length dispersion
factors.summary: The number of distinct activities and the spread of trace length (geometric std, coefficient of variation, IQR, std) load positively at about 0.73–0.96. trace_len_entropy, epa_normalized_variant_entropy, density_dfg and similarity_rate_variants load negatively. Logs with a larger alphabet tend to have sparser DFGs and more varied trace lengths. The factor mixes two notions, and trace_len_max, trace_len_std, trace_len_variance and the global block entropies cross-load with Factor 2 or Factor 1.

factors.name: Concentration of start and end activities
factors.summary: High frequencies per start and end activity, n_cut_vertices_dfg and separability_ratio_dfg load at about 0.81–0.97. The counts of unique start and end activities and start_activities_std load at about -0.78 to -0.80. Logs with few distinct start and end activities score high, and their DFGs have more cut vertices.

factors.name: DFG size and connectivity
factors.summary: The DFG edge counts, cyclomatic number, maximum node degree and connectivity, together with number_of_successions, load only moderately (0.58–0.65). All of them cross-load on Factor 1 at 0.53–0.56. Several of these measures are linearly dependent, so the factor is partly a redundancy artefact.

factors.name: Loops within traces
factors.summary: All loop measures of the Repetitions group load clearly (0.61–0.88) and nothing else loads strongly. The factor captures how often and how long traces loop. n_traces_with_repetition does not belong here; it loads instead on Factor 2 (0.58).

factors.name: Start activity dominance
factors.summary: Only start_activities_variance (0.68) and start_activities_max (0.60) load here, with start_activities_std at 0.55. start_activities_variance also loads -0.60 on Factor 4. The factor appears to reflect a dominant start activity but is weak, carrying 1.8% of the variance.

factors.name: End activity spread
factors.summary: end_activities_std (0.80) and end_activities_variance (0.79) form a two-measure factor, with end_activities_max at 0.37. It reflects unequal frequencies of end activities and explains 1.6% of the variance.

factors.name: Trace comparison structure
factors.summary: Only structure is assigned (0.71), with mean_variant_occurrence (-0.68, equally on Factor 1) and rel_unique_end_activities (-0.41). The definition of structure gives only its group (Trace comparison), so its meaning is not interpreted further.

factors.name: Shape of activity frequencies
factors.summary: activities_kurtosis (-0.70) and activities_skewness (-0.61) load negatively. High scores therefore mean a less skewed, less peaked distribution of activity occurrences. This is a weak two-measure factor.

factors.name: Weak trace length histogram factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. The largest loadings are moderate: trace_len_hist9 at 0.52 and several other histogram bins and eventropy_lempel_ziv_flattened at 0.32–0.39, most of them measures with low communality. It should not be interpreted substantively.

factors.name: Trace length histogram bins 4 and 7
factors.summary: Two histogram bins of trace length load highly (0.87, 0.83) and nothing else does. The factor likely reflects a specific trace length pattern in the generated logs rather than a general dimension.

factors.name: Weak sequentiality and similarity factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. Only moderate loadings appear: sequentiality_ratio_dfg 0.48, similarity_rate_variants 0.39, average_affinity 0.37, separability_ratio_dfg 0.33. A loose link between sequential DFGs and similar traces is possible but not well supported.

factors.name: Trace length histogram extremes
factors.summary: trace_len_hist1 (0.89) and trace_len_hist10 (0.75) load together, suggesting mass in the outer bins of the trace length histogram. The factor is narrow and explains 1.3% of the variance.

factors.name: Trace length histogram shape
factors.summary: The skewness and kurtosis of the trace length histogram load at about 0.70, and both also load about 0.48–0.53 on Factor 3. The factor captures asymmetry and peakedness of the trace length distribution but rests on two measures.

factors.name: Frequency of rare activities
factors.summary: activities_min (0.52) is the only assigned measure, with activities_q1 (0.44) and activities_median (0.32) below threshold. The factor may reflect how often the least frequent activities occur, but it is weak.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.93. The 16 varimax factors explain 89% of the variance, but the first four carry about 69%. These four are variant diversity/entropy, log volume and trace length, activity alphabet with trace length dispersion, and start/end activity concentration. Two further clear factors cover DFG size/connectivity and loops. Factors 7–16 each explain under 2% of the variance and rest on one or two measures, often histogram bins or variance/std pairs, or have no assigned measure at all (Factors 11 and 13). A smaller factor count would likely give a more robust solution.
caveats: The correlation matrix is singular because several measures are linearly dependent, e.g. n_edges_dfg, cyclomatic_number_dfg and number_of_successions, so results rely on pseudo-inverses.
n_events, mean_variant_occurrence and average_edit_distance reach communalities near 1, a possible Heywood case.
Measure definitions give only the group name, so interpretations rest on measure names and group descriptions, not exact formulas.
n_traces is constant in this dataset, so count-based measures partly stand in for ratios, and this may not generalise to other log collections.
Many measures cross-load, notably the DFG measures on Factors 5 and 1 and the trace length spread measures on Factors 2 and 3, which blurs the separation of these factors.
trace_len_hist2/3/5/8/9, end_activities_max, average_affinity, sequentiality_ratio_dfg and cyclicity_dfg remain unassigned.
Varimax forces orthogonal factors, and the solution depends on this dataset, the rotation and the chosen number of 16 factors.
